! Finds all Narcissistic (or Armstrong) numbers between 100 and 999.
! A Narcissistic number is a three-digit number where the sum of the cubes of its digits equals the number itself.
! For example, 153 is a Narcissistic number because 153 = 1^3 + 5^3 + 3^3.

! Returns:
! - An array of integers containing all the Narcissistic numbers between 100 and 999.

! Example:
! - find_narcissistic_numbers() returns [153, 370, 371, 407]
function find_narcissistic_numbers() result(narcissistic_nums)
source_record.canonical_solution:
integer, dimension(:), allocatable :: narcissistic_nums
  integer :: i, count, digit, sum, temp
  integer, dimension(:), allocatable :: temp_arr
  integer, dimension(:), allocatable :: new_arr
  count = 0
  allocate(temp_arr(5))
  
  do i = 100, 999
      sum = 0
      temp = i
      ! Extract and cube each digit
      do while (temp > 0)
          digit = mod(temp, 10)
          sum = sum + digit**3
          temp = temp / 10
      end do

      ! Check if number is a Narcissistic number
      if (sum == i) then
          count = count + 1
          if (count > size(temp_arr)) then
              ! Resize the array by allocating a new one and moving data    
              allocate(new_arr(size(temp_arr) + 5))
              new_arr(:size(temp_arr)) = temp_arr
              call move_alloc(from=new_arr, to=temp_arr)
          end if
          temp_arr(count) = i
      end if
  end do

  ! Allocate the exact size for the result
  allocate(narcissistic_nums(count))
  narcissistic_nums = temp_arr(:count)
end function find_narcissistic_numbers

    integer :: year, month, day

    days_in_month = (/ 31, 28, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31 /)

    read(date_string(first_slash_pos+1:second_slash_pos-1), *) month

function longest_common_subsequence_length(str1, str2, length1, length2) result(lcs_length)

! Arguments:
! - arr: An integer array that needs to be sorted.

! - right: The ending index of the array/sub-array.

! Example:
! - Given an array arr = [5, 2, 6, 1, 7, 3, 4], calling quick_sort(arr, 1, size(arr)) will sort the array in ascending order.
recursive subroutine quick_sort(arr, left, right)
source_record.canonical_solution:
integer, intent(inout) :: arr(:)
    integer, intent(in) :: left, right
    integer :: pivot, i, j, temp

    if (left < right) then
        pivot = left
        i = left
        j = right

        do while (i < j)
            do while (arr(i) <= arr(pivot) .and. i < right)
                i = i + 1
            end do

            do while (arr(j) > arr(pivot))
                j = j - 1
            end do

            if (i < j) then
                temp = arr(i)
                arr(i) = arr(j)
                arr(j) = temp
            end if
        end do

        temp = arr(pivot)
        arr(pivot) = arr(j)
        arr(j) = temp

        call quick_sort(arr, left, j - 1)
        call quick_sort(arr, j + 1, right)
    end if
end subroutine quick_sort

! It takes a list of IDs and the total number of IDs as input, and returns both the missing and duplicate ID.
!
! Arguments:
! - ids: An array of integers representing the ticket IDs.
! - n: The total number of ticket IDs.
!
! Returns:
! - missing_id: The ID that is missing in the sequence.
! - duplicate_id: The ID that appears more than once in the sequence.
!
! Example:
! Given IDs: [5, 6, 8, 11, 9, 10, 12, 9]
! The subroutine would return missing_id = 7 and duplicate_id = 9, as 7 is missing and 9 is duplicated.
subroutine find_missing_and_duplicate_ids(ids, n, missing_id, duplicate_id)
source_record.canonical_solution:
integer, intent(in) :: ids(:), n
    integer, intent(out) :: missing_id, duplicate_id
    integer :: sorted_ids(n), i

    ! Copy and sort the input array to avoid modifying the original array
    sorted_ids = ids
    call sort(sorted_ids, n)

    ! Initialize output variables
    missing_id = -1
    duplicate_id = -1

    ! Iterate through sorted array to find duplicate
    do i = 1, n - 1
        if (sorted_ids(i) == sorted_ids(i + 1)) then
            duplicate_id = sorted_ids(i)
            exit
        end if
    end do

    ! Calculate the expected sum of the sequence and find the missing ID
    missing_id = ((sorted_ids(n) * (sorted_ids(n) + 1)) / 2) - &
                 ((sorted_ids(1) * (sorted_ids(1) - 1)) / 2) - &
                 (sum(sorted_ids) - duplicate_id)

end subroutine find_missing_and_duplicate_ids

subroutine sort(array, n)
    integer, intent(inout) :: array(:)
    integer, intent(in) :: n
    integer :: i, j, min_idx, temp

    do i = 1, n - 1
        min_idx = i
        do j = i + 1, n
            if (array(j) < array(min_idx)) then
                min_idx = j
            end if
        end do
        temp = array(i)
        array(i) = array(min_idx)
        array(min_idx) = temp
    end do
end subroutine sort
